CORAM:
 HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SHALINDER KAUR  ORDER % 08.07.2025 CRL.M.A. 19089/2025(Exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

The present appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 415(2) read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, assailing the Judgment dated 23.09.2024 and Order on Sentence dated 02.12.2024 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-06 (West District), Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi in Sessions Case No. 32/2019 titled as "State vs.
Bhagwan Dass" arising out of the FIR No. 452/2018 for offences punishable under Sections 363/366/376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ("POCSO Act") registered at Police Station Nangloi.

The learned counsel for the appellant submits the appellant was convicted for the aforesaid offences and vide the Order on Sentence, he was sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for period of twenty years and to pay a fine of Rs. 15,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to undergo Simple Imprisonment for a period of one year for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

The appellant was also sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for a period of three years and to pay a fine of Rs. 5,000/- and in default of payment of fine, to undergo Simple Bhagwan Dass vs State (Nct Of Delhi) on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147518138/

sentences.text: Imprisonment for a period of six months for the offence punishable under Section 363 of the IPC.

5. The learned counsel submits that pursuant to a missing report lodged by the mother of the prosecutrix, who was 13 years of age at the time of the incident, the present FIR was registered on 17.11.2018 against the appellant.

6. During the course of investigation, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("CrPC"), and upon consideration of the evidence collected by the Investigating Agency, a Charge-Sheet was filed.
Thereafter, charges were framed against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 366 and 376 of the IPC, and Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

7. The learned counsel submits there are material contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimony of PW-1, inasmuch as, in her statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC, she exonerated the appellant and stated that she had accompanied him of her own free

8. He submits that there is a serious doubt with respect to the actual age of the prosecutrix, as the school records produced during the trial reflect her date of birth based solely on the declaration made by her mother, and not on the basis of any valid birth certificate or documentary evidence.
He further submits that the appellant has been languishing in custody since 07.12.2018.
9. Issue notice.
10. Mr. Satish Kumar, the learned APP, accepts notice and seeks time to file a status report.

11. Let the status report be filed, at least three days prior to the next date of hearing, with an advance copy to the opposite side.
12.

Let the nominal roll of the appellant be requisitioned, from the concerned Jail Superintendent,
before the next date of hearing.

13. In view of the mandate of the Supreme Court in Jagjeet Singh & Ors. vs. Ashish Mishra @ Monu & Anr. (2022) 9 SCC 321, intimation be issued through the IO/SHO to the prosecutrix, who may either appear in person or through video conferencing, or be represented through an Advocate, on the next date of hearing.
